slowest_experiments.experiment: V632 exact Markdown and YAML task-contract preflight

summary: Two experiments completed in 0.3 minutes, including one compute-bound experiment. The synthesis-only contract preflight took 0.28 minutes, while Qwen3.8 claim/evidence structured trace capture was the sole and therefore longest compute-bound experiment at 0.01 minutes. The locked task-conditioned field records no compute-bound GPU-idle condition.
bottlenecks_identified: V632 exact Markdown and YAML task-contract preflight was the longest observed entry at 0.28 minutes, but no data available this milestone explains its phase cost; its synthesis-only status means GPU inactivity is expected.
Disk-mtime reconstruction ranks the two entries but supplies no phase-level timing for the 0.01-minute compute-bound trace capture.
No data available this milestone establishes a two-or-more-model parallel launch or a missed DualGPURunner dispatch.
improvements_suggested: Cache exact Markdown and YAML contract-preflight results by content and validator version.
Emit high-resolution monotonic timestamps for each task phase instead of relying only on disk modification times.
Sample GPU utilization during each compute-task window and attach task and process ownership to every sample.
Record concurrent model count and runner selection in each compute launch receipt; select DualGPURunner only when two or more models run in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add content-addressed caching for the exact Markdown and YAML contract preflight.
Add a task-scoped telemetry envelope with phase clocks and in-window GPU samples.
Persist model-count and runner-selection evidence for every compute launch.
meta_reflection: The timing data identifies the synthesis preflight as the largest observed cost, but it does not identify a causal phase. The GPU report shows idle devices, yet the locked task-conditioned indicator is false, so compute-window GPU efficiency and any numeric savings remain unproven.
